definitions.explanation: Overseeing and checking the content of a publication, program, or project to ensure accuracy and quality. The person who does this is the {監修者|かんしゅうしゃ}.

examples.japanese: この{本|ほん}は{専門家|せんもんか}が{監修|かんしゅう}した。
examples.english: This book was supervised by an expert.

examples.japanese: {有名|ゆうめい}なシェフ{監修|かんしゅう}のメニューが{登場|とうじょう}した。
examples.english: A menu supervised by a famous chef appeared.

examples.japanese: {医師|いし}の{監修|かんしゅう}のもとで{作|つく}られた{健康|けんこう}{食品|しょくひん}なので{安心|あんしん}して{食|た}べられる。
examples.english: Since the health food was made under the supervision of a doctor, you can eat it with confidence.

notes:
USAGE:
Used both as a suru verb ({監修|かんしゅう}する, to supervise) and as a noun modifier ({監修|かんしゅう}の). Very common in publishing, media, and product marketing to indicate expert oversight. Often seen on book covers and food packaging: 〇〇{監修|かんしゅう} (supervised by 〇〇).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {医師|いし}{監修|かんしゅう}: supervised by a doctor
- {監修者|かんしゅうしゃ}: supervisor, editorial supervisor
- {監修|かんしゅう}のもとで: under the supervision of
- ～が{監修|かんしゅう}する: ~ supervises

HOMOPHONE:
- {慣習|かんしゅう}: custom, convention (different meaning)
